title: Trade the Event: Corporate Events Detection for News-Based Event-Driven Trading

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper introduces a bi-level event-driven trading strategy that detects corporate events from news articles to forecast short-term stock price movements. A low-level sequence labeling detector identifies event tokens while a high-level classifier integrates article-level context and low-level predictions. Recognized events are mapped to long or short positions immediately upon news publication and traded using policies such as holding for a fixed number of days or closing at the best price.
extraction.data_period: Mar 1st, 2020 - Apr 30th, 2021 (Newswire) and Aug 16th, 2020 - May 6th, 2021 (Businesswire), minute-level timestamps
extraction.universe: Securities listed on NYSE and NASDAQ
key_findings: Corporate events provide a higher signal-to-noise ratio and better average returns for stock prediction compared to traditional news sentiment analysis.
The proposed bi-level event detection model outperforms baseline architectures (such as Sentence-level and CRF models) across winning rates, excess returns, and average returns.
Timeliness is critical for event-driven strategies; delaying trade execution by even tens of seconds after publication heavily impairs performance and leads to negative average returns.

Different corporate events exhibit distinct price movement patterns and profitability ceilings (e.g., Special Dividends and Reverse Stock Splits are highly profitable, whereas Dividend Increases have minimal impact).
limitations: Assumes the cost of time in acquiring news and executing trades is almost zero.
Assumes unlimited stock liquidity, ignoring potential market impact and liquidity constraints as investment scales up.
Imperfect ticker recognition may occasionally introduce noise or point to incorrect securities.
